oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and documents them as interchangeable.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical access_token and id_token contents as token confusion by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: When using session-based authentication with the MCP server, scope checks are bypassed and full tool access is granted.
oidc_jwt.note: Use Bearer tokens for scope-enforcement tests; cookie-auth full access is expected.

oidc_jwt.description: The /api/userinfo response only includes claims allowed by the granted scope.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing profile/email fields without corresponding scopes is expected, not an identity truncation bug.

oidc_jwt.description: The /api/userinfo response only includes claims allowed by the granted scope.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing profile/email/phone claims are expected unless those scopes were requested and granted.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor documents standard OAuth/JWT bearer-token usage and does not document jti replay prevention for normal access tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same bearer token is by design for stateless validation and should not be reported as a replay vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: On SSO logout, Casdoor invalidates tokens by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value, and introspection/refresh reject tokens with ExpiresIn <= 0.
oidc_jwt.note: Post-logout token rejection is expected and tied to token metadata invalidation rather than cryptographic revocation lists.

oidc_jwt.description: Using authorization_code grant with code=guest-user creates a guest account instead of completing a normal OAuth code flow.
oidc_jwt.note: This is a documented Casdoor extension and should not be mistaken for arbitrary code acceptance.

oidc_jwt.description: Shared applications use organization-specific identifiers by appending -org-<organizationName> to the client_id or application name.
oidc_jwt.note: Different org-specific client IDs derived from one shared application are expected and should not be treated as cross-tenant confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: For SAML providers, if username mapping is absent or empty, Casdoor falls back to email and then NameID for username construction.
oidc_jwt.note: Username differences caused by documented fallback logic are by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor can lowercase usernames when isUsernameLowered is enabled.
oidc_jwt.note: Case-collapsing under this setting is expected behavior, not necessarily an identity-binding bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and treats them as interchangeable for authentication and authorization.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical access_token and id_token contents as token confusion by itself; this is documented behavior.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Casdoor's token endpoint accepts JSON request bodies in the documented examples for authorization_code, password, client_credentials, refresh_token, and token-exchange grants. The fuzzer MUST send JSON to /api/login/oauth/access_token for these flows; using form encoding may not match the documented API usage.

For authorization code flows with RFC 8707 resource indicators, the resource parameter MUST match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. If the values differ, audience-binding tests are invalid because Casdoor documents exact matching between authorization and token requests.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL flow using a valid token request in the same application configuration. Without a successful control login, a failed attack login cannot be distinguished from bad client_id, redirect_uri, or grant-type setup.

Casdoor supports PKCE on the authorization code flow. When testing PKCE-related I3 behavior, the fuzzer MUST send code_challenge_method=S256 and code_challenge at authorize time, then send the matching code_verifier at token exchange time. If PKCE is enabled for the application and code_verifier is omitted or wrong, token exchange failure is expected and not evidence of another invariant violation.

For public/native-style OIDC clients using PKCE, Casdoor documents that client_secret becomes optional, but if provided it must be correct. The fuzzer MUST either omit client_secret entirely or send the exact configured secret; sending an incorrect secret produces a by-design failure.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo returns claims according to the granted scope. I4/I5 verification logic MUST request the needed scopes during authorization first; missing email/profile/phone claims in /api/userinfo are by design when those scopes were not granted.
Casdoor documents that access_token and id_token are the same JWT payload and can be used interchangeably. This is by design and MUST NOT be flagged as token confusion or over-issuance by itself.

Refresh token lifetime has a numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. The fuzzer MUST treat value 0 as a configured default/disabled-like application setting rather than assuming a positive lifetime. Freshness tests that rely on refresh tokens should explicitly configure a nonzero refresh lifetime when possible.

Application Code resend timeout has a numeric sentinel: value 0 means use the global default rather than literal zero-second resend. Do not assume 0 disables waiting or creates immediate resend behavior.

Application CookieExpireInHours has a numeric sentinel: value 0 means use the default cookie lifetime rather than immediate expiry. Session-freshness tests must not interpret 0 as an already-expired session.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Casdoor documents that omitting scope causes the exchanged token to inherit the subject token's scope, while specifying scope is intended for narrowing. The fuzzer MUST request a strictly smaller scope set than the original when testing downscoping; requesting broader scopes is the attack case.

For I5 token exchange audience/scope tests, Casdoor supports subject_token_type values access_token, jwt, and id_token. The fuzzer MUST set subject_token_type explicitly to match the actual token being exchanged; otherwise failures may be due to token-type mismatch rather than audience or authorization binding.

Casdoor's token introspection endpoint is protected by HTTP Basic authentication using client_id:client_secret. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection with the application credentials, not the bearer token under test, or introspection failures will be misinterpreted.

Casdoor supports stateless JWT/OAuth bearer tokens and does not document jti replay tracking for ordinary access tokens. replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti are hardening checks only and MUST NOT be reported as I2 vulnerabilities for standard bearer-token reuse.
For OIDC callback and redirect-uri tests, redirect_uri must exactly match an application's configured Redirect URL. redirect_uri_mismatch failures are expected setup errors, not flow-coherence bugs.

Shared applications alter client_id semantics: when IsShared is enabled, the effective client_id may be the base client_id with suffix -org-<organizationName>. Cross-tenant and audience-binding tests MUST account for this org-specific client_id transformation or they will target the wrong audience/client.

Casdoor supports wildcard redirect URIs for localhost callback patterns in some MCP/OAuth client scenarios (for example http://127.0.0.1:*/callback). Tests that compare redirect_uri values MUST distinguish documented wildcard registration behavior from arbitrary redirect acceptance.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo accepts the access token either as Bearer Authorization or as query parameter accessToken. Verification sequences should prefer Bearer-token usage for consistency, but query-parameter acceptance is documented behavior and not a credential leakage bug by itself.

For I3 authorization-code flow tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the same redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth when the flow was initiated with a redirect_uri. Casdoor documentation states the provider callback URL and Casdoor redirect URL are distinct, and OAuth clients are configured around exact callback URLs; mismatched callback handling will cause legitimate flow rejection rather than a coherence bug.

For I5 audience-binding tests using RFC 8707 resource indicators, start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token MUST both include the same resource value. Casdoor states the resource must match exactly between authorization and token requests, and the resulting access token aud becomes the resource URI instead of the client_id.

For I2 freshness tests on refresh tokens, application parameter RefreshExpireInHours has sentinel semantics: default 0 hours means refresh is effectively disabled/expired unless explicitly configured to a positive lifetime. Never assume 0 means unlimited. Configure a positive refresh lifetime before testing refresh-based sequences.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control login using a valid token or valid authorization-code exchange in the same setup. A failed login without a control may be caused by application grant-type settings, redirect URI mismatch, or missing client configuration rather than token time validation.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, request an exchanged scope that is a strict superset of the original scope and verify the returned scope/claims do not expand. Casdoor documents that omitted scope inherits the subject token scope and that specified scope is intended for narrowing; tests that omit scope are not valid escalation probes.

For I1/I5 token exchange audience tests on Casdoor, use the resource parameter as the audience control because Casdoor documents RFC 8707 resource indicators and sets aud to the resource URI. When testing wrong-audience acceptance, compare tokens minted with different resource URIs and do not rely only on client_id differences.

For OIDC/OAuth callback tests involving PKCE, if code_challenge/code_challenge_method were sent in start_oidc_auth then exchange_code_for_token MUST include the original code_verifier. Casdoor documents PKCE support and states client_secret becomes optional only when PKCE is used correctly; missing code_verifier causes legitimate exchange failure, not a security finding.

For I3 config-change tests involving application settings, changes to grant types, redirect URIs, PKCE, token format, or resource binding affect NEW logins by design. A valid coherence test must show inconsistent handling of the same request under unchanged config, not that an admin legitimately changed application behavior between attempts.

For multi-tenant tests, Casdoor resource ownership semantics are not uniform across concepts: users belong to exactly one organization, while applications are owned/configured within an organization and shared applications are created only by built-in. The fuzzer MUST use the correct organization/owner values per resource type and MUST NOT assume one global owner field works for users and applications interchangeably.

For I4 cross-user collision tests, account linking by external OAuth identity, email/phone, or username is a documented feature. When testing identity collapse, distinguish by-design linking from unintended collisions; collisions caused by configured automatic account linking are not proof of a broker bug.

For I4 case-confusion tests on usernames, server setting isUsernameLowered controls whether usernames are converted to lowercase. If enabled, case variants may collapse by design; the fuzzer must record this setting before treating case-folding as an identity-binding violation.

For I4 tests involving email-as-username, organization setting Use email as username causes username to track email when the username field is hidden. Different identities that share or change email may therefore affect downstream naming by design; use stable user ID/sub rather than displayed username alone as the oracle.

For I2 session revocation tests, revoke_session maps to /api/sso-logout and revokes the currently authenticated session (or all sessions when logoutAll is true); it does not accept an explicit token value. The fuzzer MUST call it with the target session token itself and MUST NOT expect admin-driven arbitrary token revocation semantics.

For I2 logout invalidation tests, Casdoor invalidates tokens on SSO logout by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value, and introspection/refresh reject tokens with ExpiresIn <= 0. Treat post-logout refresh failure as by-design token invalidation, and use introspect_token or protected API access to confirm revocation state.

For I5 scope-based authorization tests against MCP or other scoped APIs, session-based authentication bypasses scope checking and grants full access by design. The fuzzer MUST use Bearer access tokens, not browser session cookies, when testing scope enforcement.

For I5 custom-scope tests, only Agent-category applications support custom scopes. Default-category applications expose only standard OIDC scopes. The fuzzer MUST create or use an Agent application when testing custom scope issuance or enforcement.

For I1/I5 audience tests on MCP/resource servers, the aud claim must match the MCP server resource URI exactly, including scheme, host, and port. A 401 caused by aud mismatch is expected behavior and should not be treated as a bug in token issuance or identity mapping.

For I3 single-session tests, application setting EnableExclusiveSignin intentionally removes all existing sessions for the same user and application on each new sign-in. Concurrent-session invalidation under this setting is by design and must not be reported as a coherence flaw.

For I5 application-tag authorization tests, application tags restrict sign-in to users whose tags intersect the application's tags, while admins and global admins bypass this restriction by design. Do not use admin accounts as negative controls for tag-based denial tests.

For I1/OIDC request-object tests, the provided Casdoor documentation does not document support for a request JWT parameter on /login/oauth/authorize even though generic OIDC may allow it. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume request-object processing exists unless discovered separately; failures or ignored request parameters are inconclusive for oidc_request_object_alg_none.

Casdoor's token endpoint expects JSON request bodies in the documented examples for authorization_code, password, client_credentials, refresh_token, token_exchange, and guest-user flows. The fuzzer MUST send application/json to /api/login/oauth/access_token for these flows; sending form data may not match the documented API usage.

For I3 PKCE tests, when code_challenge/code_challenge_method=S256 are sent to /login/oauth/authorize, the token request to /api/login/oauth/access_token MUST include the original code_verifier. With PKCE enabled, client_secret becomes optional, but if provided it must be correct.

For RFC 8707 audience/resource binding tests, if the authorization request includes resource, the token request MUST include the same resource value exactly. Casdoor documentation states the resource must match exactly between authorization and token requests; otherwise failures are setup errors, not security findings.

For I5 audience-binding tests on authorization-code flow, Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI when the resource parameter is supplied; otherwise aud is the client_id. The fuzzer MUST choose the expected oracle based on whether resource was requested.

For I2 freshness tests (expired_token, future_token, nbf), the sequence MUST include a control login using a valid token or valid authorization flow alongside the attack case. Without a control, token rejection cannot be distinguished from broken application/client configuration.

Refresh token lifetime has sentinel semantics: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. In Casdoor, default 0 hours is a configured default value, not evidence of immediate expiry semantics for all contexts. The fuzzer MUST treat 0 as a special configured default and explicitly set nonzero refresh lifetimes when testing refresh behavior.

On SSO logout, Casdoor invalidates tokens by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value. Introspection and refresh reject tokens with ExpiresIn <= 0. For logout-related I2 tests, post-logout token failure is BY DESIGN and should be checked via introspection active=false or refresh rejection, not treated as inconsistent token parsing.

For verify_granted_identity, Casdoor supports both Bearer Authorization header and query parameter accessToken. The fuzzer SHOULD prefer Bearer header for normal session inspection and use query mode only when explicitly testing alternate credential transport semantics.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Casdoor documentation states that requested scope should be a subset of the original token's scope, and omitting scope inherits the subject token scope. The fuzzer MUST compare exchanged-token claims/scopes against the original authorization and treat inherited scope on omitted scope as expected behavior.

Casdoor supports subject_token_type values access_token, jwt, and id_token for token exchange. The fuzzer MUST set subject_token_type explicitly in token exchange tests so failures are not misattributed to unsupported token-type defaults.

For OIDC callback and redirect_uri coherence tests, redirect_uri must exactly match one of the application's configured Redirect URLs. Any mismatch causes a legitimate setup failure rather than an I3 issue.

Casdoor supports wildcard redirect URIs with * for localhost callback ports in some MCP/desktop client documentation (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:*/callback). This wildcard behavior is application-configuration specific; the fuzzer MUST only rely on wildcard redirect matching when the application is explicitly configured that way.
For DCR-based setups, /api/oauth/register requires at least one redirect_uris entry. Registration failures due to missing redirect_uris are setup errors, not security findings.
Dynamic Client Registration can be disabled per organization via dcrPolicy. The fuzzer MUST verify DCR is enabled before treating registration failure as a protocol issue.

Casdoor's token introspection endpoint /api/login/oauth/introspect is protected by HTTP Basic authentication using client_id:client_secret. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection with client credentials; Bearer access tokens are not the documented auth mode for this endpoint.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise. MULTI-APP SEQUENCES: When a test needs two separate applications (e.g., token exchange between different clients/audiences), use app-test as the SOURCE application (already exists) and create ONE new application as the TARGET. Create users with signupApplication matching the app they will login to. For login_with_password, the executor auto-resolves client_id from the user signupApplication — so set signupApplication correctly in create_user.
